judge_assessment.explanation: I solved all twelve systems independently and every solution, determinant and contextual unit the judge cites is correct: (75, 45) tickets; 8 L and 4 L of acid; det A = 7 with (2, 5) dollars; det A = -11 with 12 and 24 seats via Cramer; the parabola-line meeting at (2,3) and (4,7); k=5, c=1 km/h from k+c=6 and k-c=4; det A = -10 with 3 chairs and 5 tables; the circle-line crossings (3,4) and (-4,-3); $1500 and $2500; det A = 0 with an inconsistent pair (doubling sheet one gives 4x+6y=24 against sheet two's 30); a 7 m by 10 m garden; and 80/80/40 concert tickets. The judge's manual review of problem 10 is also exactly right. What the judge did not open is the generated Quick Answers bank, and it is broken in two places. Entry 10 prints '10. 0,' - a determinant followed by a dangling comma and nothing else - because verify.json id 10's inconsistent system declares "expected": [] and render_quick_answers._fmt maps an empty list to the empty string (scripts/render_quick_answers.py: 'if isinstance(v, list): return ", ".join(_fmt(x) for x in v)'). The answer 'no solution', which is the entire point of problem 10 and the only place the sheet teaches what a zero determinant means, is silently dropped from the grading bank. Entries 3, 4 and 7 print the determinant as an unlabelled trailing number beside labelled variables - '3. x = 2, y = 5, 7' - so a grader has to infer that the loose 7 is det A.

strengths_to_preserve: Problem 10 is the best item in the set and is built correctly end to end: the caterer's two order sheets are proportional in the coefficients but not in the totals, so det A = 0 is verified as an eval, the system is verified with "expected": [] (no solution), and the interpretation is a separate declared manual entry. The key then distinguishes the two zero-determinant outcomes explicitly - 'Had sheet two read 24 servings, the determinant would still be 0, but then the two sheets would agree and there would be infinitely many solutions instead of none.'

The interleave is real rather than nominal: after two context-to-system warm-ups the sheet alternates matrix/Cramer items (3, 4, 7, 10), nonlinear intersections (5, 8, 11) and further context systems (6, 9), finishing with a three-variable synthesis (12) - so method choice, not method repetition, is what the sheet exercises.

Every solution in the key ends by substituting back into the ORIGINAL context equations, including the ones where the check is cheap to skip: '0.05(1500) + 0.08(2500) = 75 + 200 = 275', 'perimeter 2(7) + 2(10) = 34, area 7 x 10 = 70', '12(80) + 8(80) + 5(40) = 1800'. The worksheet's own directions demand that habit, and the key models it twelve times out of twelve.
Problem 11's key resolves the two-root ambiguity in the student's favour - 'x = 7 (then y = 10) or x = 10 (then y = 7) - the same rectangle either way' - instead of arbitrarily boxing one ordering.

root_causes.description: render_quick_answers._fmt has no representation for an empty solution set. A list expected value is rendered by joining its elements, so [] renders as the empty string; render_entry then joins that with the problem's other entries and returns a truthy string ending in a dangling separator, which is neither the answer nor the '---' reserved for unchecked items.
evidence: verify.json id 10 = [eval a*d - b*c -> 0, system with "expected": [], manual explanation].
scripts/render_quick_answers.py: _fmt returns ", ".join(...) for a list, and render_entry returns text unless it is falsy - so 'no solution' becomes an empty fragment rather than words.

root_causes.description: When a problem's entries mix a dict-valued system (which renders as labelled 'var = value' pairs) with a scalar eval (which renders bare), the bank concatenates them in JSON order with no label for the scalar, so a determinant reads as a stray number appended to the solution.
evidence: answer_key.pdf Quick Answers entries '3. x = 2, y = 5, 7', '4. x = 12, y = 24, -11', '7. x = 3, y = 5, -10'.
worksheet.pdf problems 3, 4 and 7 each ask for det A in part (a) and the solution in part (b), i.e. two distinct named quantities.
scripts/render_quick_answers.py render_entry: 'text = ", ".join(_fmt(v) for v in vals)' with no per-entry label.

improvements.title: Render a verified empty solution set as words, never as an empty fragment
improvements.proposed_change: In scripts/render_quick_answers.py, make _fmt return an explicit 'no solution' rendering for an empty list (and for an empty dict), and make render_entry drop empty fragments before joining so no entry can end in a dangling separator. 'No solution' is a VERIFIED result and must be visually distinct both from a value and from the '---' that means nobody checked this. Note this is the same class as the two canonical _fmt defects (relation answers, Python builtins) - _fmt trusting a naive conversion - but it needs its own remedy, so it needs its own key.
improvements.regression_test: Unit test on render_entry: entries [{"expected": 0}, {"expected": []}, {"type": "manual"}] must render as '0, no solution' (or equivalent) and must not match /,\s*$/. Today it returns '0, ' and the assertion fails.
improvements.expected_impact: Inconsistent and dependent systems - the whole point of teaching determinants - stop vanishing from the grading bank, and no bank line ships with a trailing comma.
improvements.risk: Low. Wording must be chosen so it cannot be confused with a value; 'no solution' inside the bank should not be sympified anywhere downstream.

improvements.title: Label the determinant (and every scalar sibling) in a multi-part bank entry
improvements.proposed_change: Give render_entry a label source for non-dict entries - the simplest being an optional per-entry "label" field in verify.json ('det A', 'radius', 'c') that the bank prints as 'label = value' - and require it in SKILL.md whenever a problem id carries more than one entry of different kinds. Entry 3 would then read 'x = 2, y = 5, det A = 7'.
improvements.regression_test: Unit test: entries [{"expected": {"x": 2, "y": 5}}, {"expected": 7, "label": "det A"}] render as 'x = 2, y = 5, det A = 7'. Before the fix the label is ignored (the field is not read) and the test fails on the trailing bare 7.
improvements.expected_impact: Graders reading only the bank can tell which requested quantity each number answers - on this sheet, three of twelve entries currently require inference.
improvements.risk: Adds an optional field authors may forget; the multi-entry-per-id case is narrow enough that a verify.py advisory warning can prompt for it.

case_summary: A strong, varied systems-and-matrices synthesis set. All twelve solutions, four determinants and every contextual unit re-derived and correct; the interleave genuinely forces method choice; every key solution substitutes back into the original context; and problem 10 - two proportional order sheets whose totals disagree - is modelled exactly right, with det A = 0 verified, the system verified as having no solution, and the interpretation declared manual. The defects are entirely in the generated Quick Answers bank, which the judge did not examine. Entry 10 prints '0,' - the verified 'no solution' is dropped because _fmt maps an empty list to an empty string - so the sheet's central lesson is missing from the grading column, and entries 3, 4 and 7 append the determinant as an unlabelled loose number beside labelled variables.
